Status legend:

- `Green`: structurally aligned enough to be the stable baseline
- `Amber`: structurally close, but important fidelity or coverage gaps remain
- `Red`: missing enough structure that further refactor should be treated as mandatory

## Executive summary

The stable prompt/content, usage, request-boundary, and text-completion-family layers are now
close to AI SDK V4 shape parity.

The previous Red structural gap for AI SDK `completionModel()` is now closed on the audited
OpenAI-family paths: Siumai has a stable completion request/response family, core
trait/capability surfaces, registry handles, public facade helpers, audited OpenAI-compatible
`/completions` generate/stream support, and native OpenAI/Azure completion-family execution on the
real provider routes.

The higher-level AI SDK `uploadFile` gap is also much narrower now: Siumai has a public
`siumai::files::upload(...)` helper with explicit input/output structs, automatic media-type
detection, stable `providerReference` results, built-in adapters for the current file-capable
unified/provider clients, and public regression coverage for the main helper semantics.

Anthropic's provider-owned `files()` resource is now on that same shared contract too:
`AnthropicFiles` / `AnthropicClient` implement `FileManagementCapability`, upload/list/retrieve/
delete reuse the shared file-management structs directly, the high-level helper no longer needs an
Anthropic-only upload bridge, and the provider-local file wrapper layer is gone.

Embedding helper parity is also cleaner at the data-structure layer: the passive AI SDK import
surface now exposes `EmbedResult`, `EmbedManyResult`, `EmbedStartEvent`, `EmbedEndEvent`,
`EmbeddingModelCallStartEvent`, `EmbeddingModelCallEndEvent`, and shared response-data carriers
over the existing `Embedding`, `EmbeddingModelUsage`, `Warning`, and provider-metadata shapes.
The public facade now also has thin `siumai::embed(...)` / `siumai::embed_many(...)` helpers plus
module-level `embedding::{generate_embedding, generate_embeddings, embed_value, embed_values}`
projections over the existing embedding-family runtime, preserving raw response headers/body
without introducing a second provider execution path. The OpenAI-compatible embedding response
transformer now also carries upstream `usage.prompt_tokens` and provider-returned
`providerMetadata` through the Rust `EmbeddingResponse` metadata lane, matching the AI SDK
embedding-model result contract more closely.

Rerank helper parity now follows the same rule. The old provider-level single result item has been
renamed to `RerankRankingEntry`, so the public `RerankResult<VALUE>` name can match AI SDK's
full `rerank()` result envelope. The passive surface also exposes `RerankRanking`,
`RerankResponseMetadata`, `RerankStartEvent`, `RerankEndEvent`,
`RerankingModelCallStartEvent`, `RerankingModelCallEndEvent`, and
`RerankingModelCallRanking`. The public facade now also exposes `siumai::rerank(...)` as an
AI SDK-style JSON-value result projection, with `rerank::{rerank_result, rerank_text_result}` on the
module path for callers that want to keep the raw `rerank::rerank(...)` response surface separate.

The higher-level speech/transcription helper story is now materially closer too: stable
`TtsResponse` / `SttResponse` responses now preserve final `response` metadata and also expose
optional `warnings` plus `provider_metadata`, the shared audio executor carries that envelope
across the audited provider paths, and the public facades now return richer helper result objects
(`speech::SpeechResult`, `transcription::TranscriptionResult`) instead of exposing only the raw
provider responses. The passive AI SDK import surface now also exposes `GeneratedAudioFile`,
`DefaultGeneratedAudioFile`, `DefaultGeneratedAudioFileWithType`, `SpeechResult`,
`Experimental_SpeechResult`, `TranscriptionResult`, and
`Experimental_TranscriptionResult` as serde-aligned result envelope carriers without replacing the
Rust runtime helper structs. Successful-but-empty helper calls now also surface
`LlmError::NoSpeechGenerated` / `LlmError::NoTranscriptGenerated` instead of silently returning
empty audio/text payloads.

The earlier structural gap around AI SDK `videoModel()` is now materially narrower too: Siumai now
has a dedicated core `VideoModel` family, a registry `video_model("provider:model")` handle, a
stable `max_videos_per_call` metadata lane, and a public `siumai::video::{create_task,
query_task, wait_for_task, generate, generate_materialized}` facade. `generate(...)` now also
batches by `max_videos_per_call`, returns final generated-video assets separately from completed
tasks, auto-materializes URL-backed final videos by default, exposes an AI SDK-style first
`video` alongside `videos`, and preserves per-call plus aggregated provider metadata. The shared
request surface also now accepts prompt-less image-to-video requests through
`VideoGenerationRequest.prompt: Option<String>`, and the stable public input layer now has an
explicit `VideoGenerationPrompt` / `GenerateVideoPrompt` union that mirrors AI SDK's text-only or
image-plus-optional-text prompt shape. Provider-owned polling controls now also sit on an explicit
object-safe `VideoPollingOptions` hook, so AI SDK-style `providerOptions.*.pollIntervalMs` /
`pollTimeoutMs` values on the audited Vertex, Gemini/Google, and xAI video paths are consumed by
the high-level `siumai::video::generate(...)` polling loop instead of being sent to provider task
submission bodies. Final generated videos also expose direct `bytes()` / `base64()` accessors on
the common inline/materialized path, while `generate_materialized(...)` remains the explicit
`MaterializedVideo` normalization helper. Helper-level default URL
materialization is now intentionally limited to schemes the Rust facade can truthfully download on
its own (`data:` / `http:` / `https:`), so provider-owned URLs such as current Vertex `gs://...`
outputs remain raw URL-backed assets with warnings instead of causing false generic-download
failures. What remains open in this area is no longer model construction, batching, URL
materialization, provider-owned polling options, or the basic request shape. It is the smaller
remaining helper/runtime boundary: audited Gemini and MiniMaxi provider references now have
provider-owned materialization adapters through the shared video-family capability, while providers
that still require a different authenticated download runtime (for example current Vertex GCS-owned
outputs) remain deferred; the core Rust family also intentionally remains task-oriented instead of a
fake `doGenerate(...)` callable contract. Empty successful video runs now also surface a
specialized `LlmError::NoVideoGenerated` with final response metadata instead of falling back to a
generic parse error, which closes another higher-level parity gap against AI SDK error semantics.
Aggregated provider metadata on the video helper path now also preserves provider-root fields
beyond `videos[]` / `tasks[]`, so task-query metadata does not get flattened away during multi-call
merges. The passive AI SDK import surface now also exposes `GenerateVideoResult` over the shared
`GeneratedFile`, `VideoModelResponseMetadata`, warning, and provider-metadata carriers, matching
`generate-video-result.ts` without pretending the core provider family is a TypeScript-style
callable `doGenerate(...)` object.

Siumai now also has a public `siumai::skills::upload(...)` helper aligned with AI SDK
`uploadSkill()` on the currently audited OpenAI and Anthropic paths: explicit skill-file/result
structs, a shared `SkillsCapability` interface mirroring the provider-side `SkillsV4` shape,
provider-owned `skills()` resources, canonical `providerReference` / `providerMetadata`
shaping, Anthropic version-metadata fetch parity, and AI SDK-style OpenAI `displayTitle`
warnings are all present.

Siumai now also has a public AI SDK-style UI-message structural layer:
`siumai::types::{UiMessage, UiMessagePart, UiToolPart, ...}` plus
`siumai::ui::{validate_ui_messages, safe_validate_ui_messages, convert_to_model_messages,
convert_to_chat_request}` cover the static message shape, the `safeValidateUIMessages` result-union
path, and the `convertToModelMessages`-style conversion path. The same passive UI layer now also
exposes `CreateUIMessage`, `ChatRequestOptions`, `ChatStatus`, `ChatState`, `ChatInit`,
passive chat-transport send/reconnect option carriers, `HttpChatTransportInitOptions`, passive
prepare-request input/result carriers, `CompletionRequestOptions`, `UseCompletionOptions`,
`RequestCredentials`, `CompletionStreamProtocol`, and the UI data schema map aliases so callers can
import the stable non-runtime UI helper types without pulling in a frontend hook stack. The
upstream `ui-messages.ts` alias names (`UIMessage`, `UIMessagePart`, `TextUIPart`, `DataUIPart`,
`ToolUIPart`, `DynamicToolUIPart`, `UITool`, and related source/file/reasoning aliases) now also
resolve to the existing Rust UI carriers. The pure `ui-messages.ts` helper functions are now also
covered on the public Rust surface: UI part classifiers, static/dynamic tool-name helpers, and the
last-assistant-message completion checks for tool-call and approval-response continuations all run
over the same `UiMessage` / `UiMessagePart` carriers. The type-level inference exports that can be
honestly represented in Rust (`InferUIMessage*`, `UIMessageChunk`, `InferUIMessageChunk`,
`DataUIMessageChunk`) now resolve to the existing JSON-value, UI-message, and UI-chunk carriers.

That same UI-message layer now covers passive stream event and options data too:
`UiMessageChunk`, the named `UiMessage*Chunk` variants, `UI_MESSAGE_STREAM_HEADERS`, and
`UiMessageStreamOptions` mirror `ui-message-stream/ui-message-chunks.ts`,
`ui-message-stream-headers.ts`, and the serializable subset of
`generate-text/stream-text-result.ts`. This is intentionally limited to serde/import parity;
runtime helpers such as `createUIMessageStream`, `JsonToSseTransformStream`,
`pipeUIMessageStreamToResponse`, and function-valued stream callbacks remain deferred until Rust
owns the actual SSE/HTTP response pipeline.

What remains in this area is narrower and now clearly scoped: the intentionally absent
`useChat`-style stateful frontend hook layer plus any future provider-owned helper coverage
outside the currently audited file/skill/UI surfaces.

A bounded `types/index.ts` export audit now leaves only `EmbeddingModelMiddleware` and
`ImageModelMiddleware` as exact-name gaps in the stable type barrel. Those are function-valued
runtime callback interfaces over model calls, not passive data shapes, so they should stay deferred
until Siumai adds real embedding/image middleware execution hooks instead of exporting marker types
that are never consumed by the runtime.

The shared response-side metadata story is also materially cleaner now: `siumai-spec` exposes one
`ProviderMetadataMap` root aligned with AI SDK `ProviderMetadata` (`provider_id -> object`), and
the same shape now backs chat/completion/content/stream/file/skill response structures. The only
intentional exception is UI `providerMetadata`, which still maps onto request-side
`providerOptions` because that is how upstream `convertToModelMessages()` interprets it.

A provider-crate feature-gated compile sweep now also passes across the audited built-in and
compat-wrapped provider crates. That audit mattered because several structural drifts were
previously hidden by default-feature-only test commands: xAI file/video tests were still pinned to
older `filename` / request-extension shapes, MiniMaxi tests were still mixing the video-vs-music
`prompt` contracts, and Azure native completion metadata still instantiated `ResponseMetadata`
without the newer optional `headers` field.

The same problem also existed one layer up on the protocol/facade test surfaces. A follow-up
`all-features` sweep now passes for `siumai-core`, the three protocol crates, and top-level
`siumai`; that flush uncovered stale Anthropic protocol streaming fixtures plus top-level
experimental-bridge/transcoding tests that were still instantiating pre-`headers` response
metadata, as well as a few remaining MiniMaxi/public retry tests that still treated upload
filenames as mandatory strings.

One smaller but important shared-structure glitch is now closed too: `FinishReason::Other(String)`
serializes as a plain string again instead of Rust's default externally tagged enum object. That
matters because AI SDK stream parts always carry `finishReason.unified` as a string union,
including failed-response cases such as `"other"`. Siumai now matches that shape while still
accepting the older object form on deserialization for compatibility.

The high-level generate-text data-shape gap is also narrower now: Siumai exposes passive
`GenerateTextResult` / `GenerateTextStepResult` envelopes, a real single-step
`siumai::generate_text(...)` / `siumai::text::generate_text(...)` projection over the existing
text-family runtime, the `TextStreamPart` output union, `LanguageModelStreamPart` for the
narrower single-model-call stream lane from
`stream-language-model-call.ts`, and the AI SDK callback/event payload views from `core-events.ts`
and `tool-execution-events.ts` (`GenerateTextStartEvent`, `GenerateTextStepStartEvent`,
`GenerateTextEndEvent`, `StreamTextChunkEvent`, `ToolExecutionStartEvent`,
`ToolExecutionEndEvent`, and `ToolOutput`). The same pass now covers the pure
step-control/configuration data around `stop-condition.ts`, `filter-active-tool.ts`,
`prune-messages.ts`, `prepare-step.ts`, tool approval configuration, and tool-call repair
contexts. The tool-repair error split now follows upstream exactly at the passive data layer:
`ToolCallRepairFunctionError` carries the `NoSuchToolError | InvalidToolInputError` callback input
union, while `ToolCallRepairError` remains the separate repair-failure wrapper from
`error/tool-call-repair-error.ts`. These remain intentionally separate from runtime
`ChatStreamPart` and multi-step agent orchestration, so the structure is importable and
serde-aligned without falsely claiming full AI SDK `StreamTextResult` multi-lane runtime behavior,
the
experimental `streamLanguageModelCall` runtime helper, or serializing TypeScript callback
functions. Rust-named aliases are also present for upstream's `experimental_filterActiveTools` and
deprecated `stepCountIs` exports, and `prune_messages(...)` now covers the upstream pure
message-pruning helper over shared `ModelMessage` values. `TelemetryOptions` now also mirrors the
passive `telemetry-options.ts` fields (`isEnabled`, `recordInputs`, `recordOutputs`, `functionId`)
without claiming the callback-style `Telemetry` integration dispatcher. Runtime/function/type-level
exports such as `smoothStream`, `StreamTextTransform`, callback aliases, `OutputInterface`, and
infer helpers remain intentionally deferred until backed by real Rust behavior.

The latest bounded root-export audit leaves only runtime-owned browser/Vercel surfaces as clear
top-level gaps rather than missing passive data structures. `generateText` now has an honest
single-step Rust projection, while `streamText` still has passive event/result-carrier parity but
not the full multi-lane streaming result runtime. The AI SDK `text-stream` HTTP response helpers
now have an honest Rust server boundary through `siumai-extras::server::axum`:
`to_text_stream_response(...)` and `to_text_stream_response_with_options(...)` wrap the existing
plain text stream in an Axum `text/plain; charset=utf-8` response instead of pretending browser
`Response` or Node `ServerResponse` exist in core. The remaining AI SDK root exports
`AbstractChat`, `callCompletionApi`, and `convertFileListToFileUIParts` still belong to the
browser UI transport/state/FileList layer; `gateway` and `createGateway` belong to the separate
Vercel Gateway provider package. Siumai should not add empty marker exports for these names until
it owns the corresponding runtime contracts.

The AI SDK `error/index.ts` passive import surface is now materially closer as well. Siumai exposes
serializable carriers for the missing high-value error classes such as invalid argument/stream
part/tool approval errors, no-output/no-object/no-image/no-audio/no-video generated errors,
unsupported model-version and UI-message-stream errors, message-conversion errors, and the retry
error reason union. The provider-level error classes re-exported from `@ai-sdk/provider` are now
covered too (`APICallError`, `InvalidPromptError`, `TypeValidationError`, model/reference
resolution errors, and the simple load/content/unsupported-functionality errors). The registry
package's `NoSuchProviderError` is now covered as the matching provider-aware extension of
`NoSuchModelError` with `providerId` and `availableProviders`. The provider-utils
`DownloadError` re-export is also covered as a passive carrier for `url`, `statusCode`,
`statusText`, and serializable `cause` data, and the util download surface now has real Rust
helpers too: `create_download(...)`, `Download::download(...)`, `download_url(...)`,
`validate_download_url(...)`, `read_response_with_size_limit(...)`, and
`DEFAULT_MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE` mirror the AI SDK download safety and size-limit contract for
`http`, `https`, and inline `data:` URLs. These
intentionally mirror public error data fields and default messages without replacing Siumai's
runtime `LlmError` hierarchy or pretending that TypeScript `AISDKError.isInstance(...)` markers
exist in Rust.

The small non-browser util surface is also closer now. `SerialJobExecutor` is implemented as a
real Rust async utility backed by a FIFO `tokio::sync::Mutex`, so concurrent callers can submit
jobs while the executor polls only one job future at a time. This is deliberately separate from
Web `ReadableStream` helpers such as `consumeStream` and `simulateReadableStream`, which remain
browser/runtime stream utilities rather than core data structures.

The same passive-structure rule now covers the remaining high-value `generateObject` event data:
`GenerateObjectStartEvent`, `GenerateObjectStepStartEvent`, `GenerateObjectStepEndEvent`,
`GenerateObjectEndEvent`, `GenerateObjectResponseMetadata`, and
`GenerateObjectOutputStrategy` mirror `structured-output-events.ts`, while `ObjectStreamPart`
plus its named variants mirror the event union from `stream-object-result.ts`. This improves
import/serde parity for callback and stream-event data without claiming the full AI SDK
`StreamObjectResult` runtime object exists on the Rust facade yet.

The low-level data utility surface is also less ad hoc now: the root facade exposes
`cosine_similarity`, `get_text_from_data_url`, and `is_deep_equal_data`, matching the audited AI SDK
helper semantics while using Rust `Result` errors instead of thrown `InvalidArgumentError` /
generic JavaScript errors. The default unified prelude keeps only the application-facing subset of
these helpers; lower-level utility imports stay explicit.

Pure provider-utils HTTP/string helpers now have the same treatment where Rust can represent the
behavior honestly: `HeaderRecord`, `normalize_headers`, `normalize_optional_headers`,
`normalize_header_map`, `combine_headers`, `with_user_agent_suffix`,
`media_type_to_extension`, `strip_file_extension`, `without_trailing_slash`,
`SupportedUrlMap`, `UrlSupportRegex`, and `is_url_supported` cover the audited header
normalization/merge, user-agent suffix, media-type extension, filename stem, trailing-slash, and
URL support-table helpers. `isUrlSupported` uses a real Rust `regex`-backed typed map rather than
a fake marker export, preserving the upstream media-type wildcard/prefix behavior while avoiding
JavaScript `RegExp` runtime objects.

The pure provider-utils JSON instruction helper is now covered too. `inject_json_instruction`
matches the upstream generic-vs-schema prompt construction defaults, while
`inject_json_instruction_into_messages` rewrites the first `SystemModelMessage` or prepends one
over the stable `ModelMessage` prompt layer. This keeps the helper at the data/prompt transform
boundary and avoids coupling it to any one provider's structured-output transport mode.

Provider-utils JSON parsing now has an honest Rust equivalent as well:
`parse_json`, `safe_parse_json`, `is_parsable_json`, `parse_json_with_schema`, and
`safe_parse_json_with_schema` mirror the AI SDK parse/safe-parse split and reuse the existing
`Schema` runtime validator when a typed parse is requested. The Rust parser also rejects the same
forbidden prototype-pollution keys as upstream `secureJsonParse`, even though Rust itself is not
subject to JavaScript prototype mutation; this keeps the shared serialized data boundary aligned.

`parseProviderOptions` is now covered by `parse_provider_options`, which extracts one provider key
from the stable `ProviderOptionsMap` root and validates it through the same `Schema` runtime
validator lane. When a provider entry is absent or `null`, the helper returns `None`, matching the
upstream optional-provider-options contract. Rust does not pretend that a generic `T` can be
type-asserted without a validator, so schemas without validators return an explicit
`InvalidInput` error on this typed helper.

Provider-reference utilities are also covered without new carrier types:
`is_provider_reference` delegates to the existing `FilePartSource` source union, and
`resolve_provider_reference` resolves a provider id from `ProviderReference` while returning the
existing passive `NoSuchProviderReferenceError` carrier on misses. This matches the upstream
provider-utils behavior while keeping provider-managed files as part of the stable prompt/file
source model instead of inventing a parallel reference map.

The tool-choice surface now preserves the same two-layer shape as AI SDK. Existing Rust
`ToolChoice` remains the high-level caller input and continues to support compatibility string
serialization where provider wire adapters depend on it, while `LanguageModelV4ToolChoice` and
`prepare_tool_choice(...)` model the provider-facing V4 object contract (`{ type: "auto" }`,
`{ type: "none" }`, `{ type: "required" }`, or `{ type: "tool", toolName }`). This avoids a
breaking wire-format change while closing the model-facing data-structure gap.

The model-facing tool object layer now follows the same split. `LanguageModelV4FunctionTool`
projects from the wider `ToolFunction` while omitting user-facing `title` and `outputSchema`; its
`inputExamples` now use the upstream `{ input: ... }` item shape even when stable tools store
compatibility raw-object examples, and the provider-facing item input is now object-only like
upstream `JSONObject`. `LanguageModelV4ProviderTool` projects provider tools down to
`{ type, id, name, args }` without leaking execution ownership, schema, provider options, or
deferred-result metadata into the narrow provider-call object; its `args` carrier is now object-only
like upstream `Record<string, unknown>`. The existing `Tool` carrier remains the stable
user/runtime structure.

The provider prompt layer now has an explicit narrow projection too. `LanguageModelV4Prompt` is no
longer just a stable `ModelMessage` alias: `prepare_language_model_v4_prompt(...)` maps stable
messages into V4 provider prompt messages, wraps user/assistant text into `text` parts, converts
legacy image parts to V4 `file` parts with `image/*` fallback media type, serializes provider file
references as direct `data` maps, filters assistant `tool-approval-request` parts, preserves only
provider-executed tool approval responses with their `providerOptions`, and coalesces adjacent tool
messages. The V4 prompt/message/part overlay also validates `providerOptions` as
provider-id-keyed JSON objects, filtering wider stable `ProviderOptionsMap` entries that cannot be
represented by upstream `SharedV4ProviderOptions`. This keeps the ergonomic prompt model separate
from the actual provider prompt object expected by `language-model-v4-prompt.ts`.

`LanguageModelV4CallOptions` now gives Rust callers an explicit model-facing provider-call overlay
too: it groups the standardized prompt, projected `LanguageModelV4Tool` union, V4 tool choice,
headers, abort handle, raw-chunk intent, reasoning, response format, and provider options in the
same conceptual object as the upstream provider interface. Runtime APIs can keep using the more
ergonomic `LanguageModelCallOptions` / `RequestOptions` split without pretending that split is the
actual provider V4 call object. Its `maxOutputTokens` field now uses a provider-facing `u64`,
matching the upstream `number | undefined` width more honestly than the stable runtime settings'
`u32` compatibility slot.

The non-streaming provider result layer now has the same narrow overlay. `LanguageModelV4Content`
models the upstream generated-content union separately from high-level `GenerateTextContentPart`,
so provider-facing files use top-level `mediaType` + `data`, tool calls keep stringified JSON
`input`, provider-executed tool results use `result` / `isError`, and approval requests carry
`approvalId` plus `toolCallId` rather than the helper-level nested tool-call object. Generated
file and reasoning-file content now uses a generated-file-only `string | bytes` carrier instead of
the wider prompt `LanguageModelV4DataContent` helper, because upstream output files are
`string | Uint8Array` and do not accept URL objects. Provider-facing `tool-result.result` also
rejects `null` at the serde boundary to match upstream `NonNullable<JSONValue>`. Provider-facing
custom prompt/output overlays also validate the upstream `{provider}.{provider-type}` `kind`
shape instead of inheriting the stable custom layer's arbitrary string compatibility.
Generated `LanguageModelV4Text`, `LanguageModelV4Reasoning`, and `LanguageModelV4Source` now own
dedicated V4 overlays instead of aliasing the wider stable output/source structs, so
provider-facing `providerMetadata` can enforce upstream `SharedV4ProviderMetadata =
Record<string, JSONObject>` while stable `ProviderMetadataMap` remains compatible with wider JSON
values. `LanguageModelV4GenerateResult` groups that content with V4 finish reason, V4 usage,
provider metadata, request/response telemetry, and strict shared V4 `CallWarning` payloads; stable
legacy warning variants normalize to canonical `unsupported { feature, details }` before reaching
this AI SDK result layer. `LanguageModelV4StreamResult<STREAM>` keeps the same request/response envelope
while leaving the Rust stream carrier generic instead of pretending to be JavaScript
`ReadableStream`. The provider-facing `LanguageModelV4Usage` token carriers are
now independent `u64` structs rather than aliases to the stable `Usage` layer's `u32`
compatibility storage, so this overlay can represent upstream `number | undefined` usage counts
without constraining provider-native accounting to the high-level Rust runtime limit.

The provider-facing model interface is now explicit as well. `siumai_core::text::LanguageModelV4`
mirrors the upstream `LanguageModelV4` contract around model metadata, `supportedUrls`,
`doGenerate`, and `doStream`, with Rust method names and a concrete `LanguageModelV4Stream`
carrier for stream-part results. This closes the previous structural hole where the V4 call and
result overlays existed but no Rust trait named the provider-owned call boundary. It deliberately
does not make registry handles or the high-level `LanguageModel` helper pretend to be exact AI SDK
provider objects; providers should opt into this trait only when they expose the raw V4 contract.

The low-level stream module now keeps its payload aliases out of that standalone namespace:
experimental stream payload helpers are named `LanguageModelV4StreamToolCall`,
`LanguageModelV4StreamFile`, `LanguageModelV4StreamUsage`, and so on. This preserves the existing
`LanguageModelV4StreamPart` enum while avoiding the previous ambiguity where
`LanguageModelV4ToolCall` could mean either a standalone provider-result part with a `type` field
or an internally tagged stream payload that relies on the surrounding stream enum for the
discriminator. The stream usage payload also now treats missing token counts as upstream
`undefined` values by omitting those JSON fields rather than serializing `null`. Stream
tool-result payloads now share the same non-null result constraint, and the OpenAI Responses
custom-event bridge drops invalid null tool-result payloads before they become typed V4 parts. The
provider-facing stream union is now dedicated to V4 instead of aliasing the historical V3 union,
so every streamed `providerMetadata` field validates upstream `SharedV4ProviderMetadata =
Record<string, JSONObject>` while runtime projection filters wider stable metadata and V3
compatibility parsing stays permissive.

The provider-tool ownership gap is now closed at the shared data-structure layer. `Tool` now
serializes provider tools as AI SDK `type: "provider"` while still accepting the old
`provider-defined` discriminator on input, and `ProviderDefinedTool` now carries
`isProviderExecuted`, optional `inputSchema`, optional `outputSchema`, `args`, and
`supportsDeferredResults`. Legacy hosted-tool constructors default to `isProviderExecuted: true`,
but the new provider-defined/provider-executed constructors and
`create_provider_defined_tool_factory(...)`,
`create_provider_defined_tool_factory_with_output_schema(...)`, and
`create_provider_executed_tool_factory(...)` facades preserve the upstream distinction between
provider-defined-local-execution tools with per-call or fixed output schemas and hosted
provider-executed tools. This is a real structural carrier/factory mapping rather than a marker
export: local executors are still bound through `ExecutableTool`, while provider ownership stays on
the stable passive `Tool` shape.

The OpenAI Responses MCP fixture lane also needed a final parity refresh after the shared
provider-executed approval split stabilized: local `tool-approval-response` request fixtures now
set `providerExecuted: true` whenever the approval response corresponds to a provider-executed MCP
call, matching the current upstream `convert-to-openai-responses-input.ts` behavior and restoring
full `openai_responses_*` fixture/stream sweep parity.

Three smaller but important OpenAI-family edge fixes also landed after that sweep. First, the
shared speech surface is now semantically honest on audited JSON TTS paths: `TtsRequest.language`
actually lowers into the final request body when a provider's defaults opt into that field,
instead of remaining a stable-but-dead knob. Second, the built-in compat `groq` preset now keeps
JSON Schema structured outputs enabled by default, matching the current audited AI SDK provider
policy instead of degrading those requests to `json_object`. Third, OpenAI Responses request
conversion now omits tool-role messages whose parts are all intentionally skipped, so canonical
AI SDK histories with only non-provider-executed approval responses in a tool message no longer
fail conversion with `Tool message missing tool result`.

Anthropic custom provider ids are now closer to the audited AI SDK contract too: request parsing
can merge canonical `providerOptions.anthropic` with provider-owned custom roots such as
`my-custom-anthropic`, and top-level non-stream / finish / stream-end `providerMetadata` now
duplicates onto that custom root only when the request actually used it.

Anthropic provider-defined tool/version coverage is now also aligned more closely with the audited
AI SDK package: the shared/provider surfaces include `web_search_20260209`,
`web_fetch_20260209`, `code_execution_20260120`, and `computer_20251124`, Anthropic request
headers inject the same beta tokens as upstream for the new web/computer tools, and the 2026 web
tool path now marks implicit provider-executed `code_execution` calls as `dynamic` on the same
conditions as `hasWebTool20260209WithoutCodeExecution()`.

The Anthropic package boundary is now also closer to the audited AI SDK index at the naming layer:
the stable/provider-owned surfaces expose `AnthropicLanguageModelOptions`, deprecated
`AnthropicProviderOptions`, `AnthropicMessageMetadata`, `AnthropicUsageIteration`, and
`AnthropicToolOptions`, `AnthropicProviderSettings`, and package `VERSION`, while the stable Bedrock facade now conditionally mirrors the upstream
cross-package `AnthropicProviderOptions` re-export when both `bedrock` and `anthropic` features
are enabled. The package surface now also exports
`find_anthropic_container_id_from_last_step(...)` plus
`forward_anthropic_container_id_from_last_step(...)`, mirroring the upstream
`forwardAnthropicContainerIdFromLastStep(...)` helper over step provider metadata. Anthropic
request/tool helper writes now also merge onto existing
`providerOptions.anthropic` objects instead of overwriting sibling fields, `AnthropicMessageMetadata`
is now a dedicated narrow typed struct instead of a thin alias to the wider `AnthropicMetadata`
helper, and the tool-level runtime path now forwards `eagerInputStreaming` in addition to `deferLoading` /
`allowedCallers`.

DeepSeek now follows that same runtime-provider-root rule on the audited chat surface: request
options are read from the resolved provider namespace, response metadata is emitted under that same
root, and the typed DeepSeek helpers now expose keyed accessors for custom-root reads without
guessing arbitrary vendor aliases. DeepSeek prompt-cache usage now also mirrors the audited AI SDK
response metadata lane by projecting `usage.prompt_cache_hit_tokens` /
`usage.prompt_cache_miss_tokens` into `providerMetadata.deepseek.promptCacheHitTokens` /
`promptCacheMissTokens`, with typed helper fields for both values.

Google/Gemini request shaping is also closer to the upstream provider package now: the audited
`google|vertex` request boundary uses the runtime namespace first for request options and
`thoughtSignature` replay with the sibling namespace as fallback, matching the AI SDK fix for
mixed Google/Vertex payloads.

The helper surface tightened further on the OpenAI-family side as well: OpenAI typed metadata
helpers now expose keyed accessors for explicit provider-root reads, and the built-in Perplexity
compat preset now reshapes response metadata into the same AI SDK-style `images` /
`usage.citationTokens|numSearchQueries` / `cost` layout used by `@ai-sdk/perplexity` instead of
forwarding raw snake_case `usage/images` fragments directly.

The OpenAI typed control surface is now tighter as well: the public Rust
`OpenAILanguageModelChatOptions` now exposes `systemMessageMode`, and
`OpenAILanguageModelResponsesOptions` now exposes the audited control fields
`systemMessageMode`, `forceReasoning`, and `contextManagement`. OpenAI/Azure public option
re-exports now surface the same typed controls, and the audited `/responses` request shaper lowers
`contextManagement[].compactThreshold` onto native wire
`context_management[].compact_threshold` while keeping the control-only fields themselves off the
wire body.

The AI SDK first-class-provider gap for DeepInfra is also now closed on the audited public/runtime
paths: Siumai treats `deepinfra` as a built-in unified provider id, reuses the shared
OpenAI-compatible runtime for chat/completion/embedding, keeps provider-owned image generation/edit
routes, corrects the known DeepInfra usage-accounting drift before it reaches the stable `Usage`
layer, and now also matches the audited `createDeepInfra({ baseURL })` root-base-url semantics:
root, `/openai`, and `/inference` custom base URLs on the text-family public/config/provider-owned
paths all normalize onto the canonical `/openai` prefix instead of drifting across entrypoints.
The Rust package surface now also exposes provider-scoped
`DeepInfraChatModelId` / `DeepInfraCompletionModelId` / `DeepInfraEmbeddingModelId` /
`DeepInfraImageModelId` aliases, so DeepInfra no longer needs to fall back exclusively to the
generic compat model-id names on the public facade. The package module now also exposes
`provider_ext::deepinfra::{deepinfra(), create_deepinfra()}` as unified-provider builder helpers,
which makes the AI SDK-style package entrypoint available without having to jump back to the root
`Provider::deepinfra()` / `Siumai::builder().deepinfra()` namespaces.

The AI SDK first-class-provider gap for Vertex MaaS is now also closed on the audited public/runtime
paths: Siumai treats `vertex-maas` as a built-in unified provider id, reuses the shared
OpenAI-compatible runtime for chat/completion/embedding, derives the Vertex `/endpoints/openapi`
base URL from `project + location`, and now accepts Google Bearer auth through token providers or
preexisting `Authorization` headers instead of requiring a fake API key.

The broader Google Vertex unified-builder story is also now structurally closer to AI SDK:
`Siumai::builder().vertex()` and `Siumai::builder().anthropic_vertex()` no longer inject
provider-wide default models, because AI SDK's `createVertex()` / `createVertexAnthropic()`
construct providers and require family-specific `languageModel()` / `embeddingModel()` /
`imageModel()` calls to choose the model explicitly. The provider-owned public facade is now
closer too: `provider_ext::google_vertex::{chat, embedding, image, video, model_sets}` and
`provider_ext::anthropic_vertex::{chat, model_sets}` expose curated model constants, and the
provider catalog now reuses those same provider-owned curated subsets instead of maintaining
parallel hardcoded lists for `vertex` / `anthropic-vertex`.

The `@ai-sdk/google-vertex/anthropic` sub-entry is now also much closer at the package boundary:
Rust now exposes `GoogleVertexAnthropicProviderSettings`, `provider_ext::anthropic_vertex::{
vertex_anthropic, create_vertex_anthropic }`, the supported Vertex Anthropic tool subset under
`tools` plus `provider_tools`/`hosted_tools`, the dedicated
`GoogleVertexAnthropicMessagesModelId` type alias, and the narrower audited Anthropic typed
metadata surface (`AnthropicMessageMetadata`, `AnthropicMessageContainerMetadata`,
`AnthropicMessageContainerSkill`, `AnthropicUsageIteration`) instead of only the older wide helper.
The wrapper now also mirrors the current AI SDK structured-output contract more faithfully:
JSON-schema requests default to the reserved `json` tool fallback on the Vertex Anthropic path,
and the same effective mode is propagated into stream conversion so the public streamed/non-stream
JSON extraction behavior stays aligned across the audited 4.x and 3.7 model ids.
Its curated `models::{chat, ALL_CHAT}` subset is now also synchronized to the current upstream
model-id union rather than the older local `*-latest` aliases. More importantly, the construction
story is no longer artificially `base_url`-only on the audited paths: the provider builder,
package-level settings wrapper, and registry/unified-builder factory now all accept explicit
`project + location` or the same `GOOGLE_VERTEX_PROJECT` + `GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION` env fallback
and derive the audited `.../publishers/anthropic/models` base URL automatically. This slice is tracked under
`docs/workstreams/anthropic-vertex-package-surface-alignment/`.

Google Vertex video parity is now also materially narrower than before: the provider-owned/public
surface exposes `GoogleVertexReferenceImage`, `GoogleVertexVideoModelOptions`, deprecated
`GoogleVertexVideoProviderOptions`, `GoogleVertexVideoModelId`, and `VertexVideoRequestExt` on
top of a real Veo task runtime. The important intentional divergence from AI SDK remains the
execution shape, not the data shape: Rust keeps explicit `create_video_task` /
`query_video_task` semantics instead of inventing a fake auto-polling callable provider object,
but the shared high-level `siumai::video::generate(...)` helper now consumes typed
`pollIntervalMs` / `pollTimeoutMs` through the provider-owned `VideoPollingOptions` hook. Those
polling controls are still stripped from `predictLongRunning` task-submission bodies because they
belong to the helper/runtime loop, not the Vertex request payload.

The earlier first-class-provider gap for Cohere is now also closed on the audited public/runtime
paths: Siumai treats `cohere` as the canonical native `/v2` provider surface for
chat/embedding/rerank, requires explicit model ids on the unified builder path, and keeps the
OpenAI-compatible Cohere preset only as an opt-in compatibility story instead of the main public
contract.

The earlier first-class-provider gap for Fireworks is now also closed on the audited public/runtime
paths: Siumai treats `fireworks` as a built-in unified provider id, reuses the shared
OpenAI-compatible runtime for chat/completion/embedding/transcription, and now routes image
generation/edit through provider-owned Fireworks workflow and `image_generation` endpoints with
default image/edit fallback models plus contract/public-path coverage.

The earlier TogetherAI runtime split is now also structurally closer to the audited package
boundary: canonical `togetherai` keeps chat/completion/embedding/speech/transcription on the
shared OpenAI-compatible runtime, but image generation/edit and reranking now stay provider-owned
on the unified provider surface. Public typed `TogetherAiImageOptions` plus provider-owned image
regression coverage now pin the `/images/generations` + `image_url` edit contract instead of
reusing the generic OpenAI-compatible image lane.

The earlier Bedrock image gap is now also closed on the audited public/runtime paths: the AI SDK
Bedrock provider already exposes `image()` / `imageModel()` backed by a provider-owned
`bedrock-image-model.ts` runtime, so Siumai now also keeps Bedrock image generation on a
provider-owned `/model/{id}/invoke` lane instead of a fake unsupported boundary. `BedrockClient`,
registry metadata/factories, and public builder/config-first/registry paths now all agree on that
image family, `amazon.nova-canvas-v1:0` mirrors the upstream `maxImagesPerCall = 5` default, and
the Rust facade intentionally does not invent a public `AmazonBedrockImageModelOptions` mirror
because the upstream `packages/amazon-bedrock/src/index.ts` still does not export one.

Stable provider typing is also now structurally closer to the audited AI SDK provider package set:
`ProviderType::{Azure, Cohere, TogetherAi, Bedrock, Mistral, Fireworks, Perplexity}` now exist
alongside the previously-promoted `DeepInfra` and Google Vertex variants, so provider catalog,
retry defaults, validator heuristics, and client metadata no longer degrade those audited provider
packages to `Custom(...)`. The important nuance is now provider-specific: `mistral` and
`perplexity` still reuse the shared OpenAI-compatible runtime internally, while `fireworks` now
uses that shared runtime only for the text/audio families and keeps provider-owned image routing at
the unified provider layer.

The package-owned compat surface for `mistral` and `perplexity` is also now closer to the audited
AI SDK provider packages themselves: Mistral now has public typed language-model options
(`safePrompt`, document limits, `structuredOutputs`, `parallelToolCalls`, `reasoningEffort`)
instead of forcing raw `providerOptions.mistral` JSON, Perplexity typed options now also keep an
AI SDK-style camelCase public surface while explicit compat normalization lowers them onto
Perplexity's snake_case wire fields only at transport time, and both Mistral plus Perplexity now
reuse provider-owned curated model constants/defaults so the public catalog no longer advertises
stale Perplexity legacy ids. Their public compat facades now also expose package-level
`mistral()/create_mistral()` and `perplexity()/create_perplexity()` helper pairs directly under
`provider_ext::*`, so callers no longer need to jump out to unrelated root namespaces just to
mirror AI SDK's per-package `provider` plus `createProvider` exports.

That same package-level entry-helper rule now also holds across the audited provider-owned
facades: `provider_ext::openai::{openai, create_openai}`,
`provider_ext::anthropic::{anthropic, create_anthropic}`,
`provider_ext::azure::{azure, create_azure}`,
`provider_ext::google::{google, create_google}`,
`provider_ext::bedrock::{bedrock, create_amazon_bedrock}`,
`provider_ext::cohere::{cohere, create_cohere}`,
`provider_ext::togetherai::{togetherai, create_togetherai}`,
`provider_ext::google_vertex::{vertex, create_vertex}`,
`provider_ext::groq::{groq, create_groq}`, `provider_ext::xai::{xai, create_xai}`, and
`provider_ext::deepseek::{deepseek, create_deepseek}`, which makes the Rust facade much easier to
audit side-by-side against AI SDK package indices. The intentional exception is the generic
`openai_compatible` package: AI SDK exports `createOpenAICompatible(settings)` as a lower-level
factory, so Rust keeps that slice on `OpenAiCompatibleBuilder` / `OpenAiCompatibleConfig` /
`OpenAiCompatibleClient::from_config(...)` instead of adding a fake zero-arg package helper.

That Mistral audit is now also documented explicitly as its own package workstream:
`docs/workstreams/mistral-package-surface-alignment/` records the audited `chat + embedding`
boundary from `@ai-sdk/mistral`, the intentional lack of completion/image support, and the split
between public typed options and the lower wire contract.

The dedicated MoonshotAI compat wrapper is also now closer to the audited `@ai-sdk/moonshotai`
package boundary: canonical public/runtime identity is `moonshotai`, the old `moonshot` id is
kept only as a hidden migration alias, typed `thinking` / `reasoningHistory` request options now
normalize onto the Moonshot wire keys, curated Kimi model constants/defaults follow the audited
package subset, `provider_ext::moonshotai::{moonshotai, create_moonshotai}` now mirror the AI SDK
package-level entry helpers alongside the lower-level compat aliases, and
completion/image/embedding stay intentionally unsupported because the upstream package itself is
chat-only.

One architectural point is now explicit in the workstream baseline: AI SDK does have a shared
image abstraction through `ProviderV4.imageModel(...)`, `ImageModelV4`, and `generateImage(...)`,
so Siumai should absolutely preserve one stable image request/result surface. But that shared layer
does not imply a single generic runtime implementation. The audited upstream provider packages keep
hybrid/provider-specific image execution for Fireworks, DeepInfra, TogetherAI, Google Vertex,
OpenAI, and others, so Siumai should treat "shared interface, provider-owned runtime" as the
default image architecture unless upstream actually consolidates those execution paths. The passive
AI SDK import surface now also exposes `GenerateImagePrompt` as the upstream text-or-`images`/
`text`/`mask` prompt union, plus `GenerateImageResult` and
`Experimental_GenerateImageResult` over the existing `GeneratedFile`, image response metadata,
provider metadata, and usage carriers. `GenerateImagePrompt` can convert into the stable Rust
`GenerateImageRequest` while preserving URL/data-URL prompt inputs on the shared image input lane.

The remaining structural risk is concentrated in streaming:

- the stable stream-part shape exists
- the runtime transport has a first-class `ChatStreamEvent::Part(ChatStreamPart)` channel
- but parser/provider coverage is still incomplete
- and some protocol-native replay fields still live outside the stable model

The main raw-chunk parity gap on the audited text/completion paths is now closed: stable request
types now have a runtime-only `StreamRequestOptions.include_raw_chunks` lane, both
`siumai::text::StreamOptions` and `siumai::completion::StreamOptions` map to that lane instead of
polluting `providerOptions`, the audited OpenAI-compatible plus Anthropic chat parsers emit stable
`raw` parts in the same relative order as AI SDK (`stream-start -> raw -> response-metadata -> ...`
on the first chunk), native Bedrock Converse JSON streaming now also emits the upstream-style
Bedrock preamble (`stream-start -> response-metadata -> raw -> ...`) with stable `error` parts for
provider error envelopes, stable `text-*` / `reasoning-*` / `tool-input-*` / `tool-call` /
`finish` parts, Bedrock cache-aware usage/provider metadata on `finish`, streamed
`stopSequence` / `raw_finish_reason` retention on the final response, and response-side reasoning
metadata plus Mistral tool-call-id normalization on the non-stream lane. The audited
OpenAI-compatible plus native OpenAI/Azure completion SSE paths now also emit the same stable
lifecycle ordering on the completion lane. First-chunk parse failures are now also
narrower on the audited AI SDK lanes: OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, native OpenAI completion, and
native Cohere keep `stream-start` before optional `raw` and the parse error, native Bedrock now
keeps its first-chunk preamble before optional `raw` and the parse error, and Gemini now keeps
`stream-start` before the parse error instead of skipping the lifecycle start entirely.

The audited Bedrock request-boundary story is now also structurally closer to the AI SDK package:
`provider_ext::bedrock` now exposes typed `reasoningConfig`, `serviceTier`, and file-part
`citations` helpers instead of relying on raw `providerOptions.bedrock` JSON, unknown top-level
Bedrock passthrough fields are preserved like upstream instead of being dropped during
normalization, Anthropic Bedrock requests now derive `additionalModelResponseFieldPaths`,
`thinking`, `anthropic_beta`, and the same `maxReasoningEffort` routing split that upstream uses
(`output_config.effort`, `reasoning_effort`, or nested `reasoningConfig`), and Anthropic
structured JSON output now uses native `output_config.format` on the same audited Bedrock routes
where the AI SDK avoids the reserved JSON tool. The audited prompt converter now also keeps
message-level `cachePoint`, maps user `file` parts onto Bedrock `document` / `image` blocks with
upstream-style filename stripping plus typed document citations, replays Bedrock reasoning
`signature` / `redactedData` from canonical request-side `providerOptions`, supports tool-result
`text` + `image-data` content, and normalizes request-side Mistral tool ids on both tool calls and
tool results. On the response/public side, Bedrock reasoning parts now also have a typed metadata
view plus replay helper: `BedrockContentPartExt::bedrock_reasoning_metadata()` exposes
`signature` / `redactedData`, and `assistant_message_with_reasoning_metadata(...)` moves those
response-side fields back onto next-turn request-side `providerOptions.bedrock`.

The biggest remaining gaps are:

1. parser/provider stream-part emission is still uneven outside the already-audited
   OpenAI Responses / Anthropic / Gemini main paths plus the audited OpenAI-family completion lane
2. the runtime stream story is still split across `ChatStreamEvent`, `ChatStreamPart`, and the
   compatibility overlay even though the public naming gap is now reduced by the
   `LanguageModelV4*` aliases
3. shared non-chat request abstractions are now structurally close to the audited AI SDK shape:
   `ImageEditRequest` models typed multi-input `images[]` + `mask` semantics, and
   `ImageVariationRequest` also carries a typed file/url image input instead of a raw byte bag.
   Those typed image inputs now also expose per-input `providerOptions`, bringing the shared image
   input lane closer to AI SDK `ImageModelV4File`. A public `GenerateImageRequest` plus
   `siumai::image::generate_image(...)` helper now also restore the missing AI SDK-style unified
   image helper lane on top of the current generation/edit/variation runtimes. The public
   `GenerateImagePrompt` union now also models the upstream text-only or `{ images, text?, mask? }`
   helper prompt shape without adding a second runtime. The shared image request family exposes
   top-level `aspectRatio` plus shared `seed` across generation/edit/
   variation, compat/OpenAI image warning semantics now match the AI SDK-style
   `unsupported { feature }` lane for top-level `aspectRatio` / `seed`, xAI / Google / Vertex
   supported image paths consume those canonical shared fields directly, and the shared executor
   materializes `data:` / `http(s):` URL-backed edit/variation inputs before synchronous
   multipart/inline transformers run on the audited OpenAI/OpenAI-compatible/Vertex paths. The
   remaining follow-up work in this area is no longer the shared request shape itself; it is
   narrower provider/runtime coverage and provider-owned option parity outside that stable
   structural lane
4. the OpenAI-compatible provider-settings surface is now materially closer to AI SDK:
   `metadataExtractor`, `includeUsage`, `transformRequestBody`, `queryParams`, and an explicit
   `supportsStructuredOutputs` provider-level policy all exist on the public config/builder/runtime
   path now; the base compat default remains the conservative AI SDK `false`, while audited
   built-in wrappers such as `openrouter`, `perplexity`, `mistral`, and `groq` opt into
   `supportsStructuredOutputs = true` by default
5. the remaining high-level AI SDK helper gaps are now concentrated above the core runtime:
   Rust now has both `uploadFile` and `uploadSkill` high-level helpers, and `uploadSkill`
   additionally has a shared `SkillsCapability` plus audited OpenAI/Anthropic coverage matching
   the current AI SDK provider scope. Rust now also has a public AI SDK-style
   `UIMessage` / `convertToModelMessages` layer, so the remaining work is the final typed/pass-through
   story for provider-owned file-upload options plus the intentionally absent
   `useChat`-style stateful frontend hook layer

## Structure matrix

| Surface | AI SDK reference | Current Siumai anchor | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt message envelope | `language-model-v4-prompt.ts` | `siumai-spec/src/types/chat/message.rs`, `siumai-spec/src/types/ai_sdk.rs` | Green | Message-level `providerOptions` exists, request converters now prefer it over legacy metadata shims, the bridge-side message compaction path now preserves single-text parts when they carry canonical provider options, and the public macro/example surface has been swept to compile against that field. The V4 provider-facing overlay now also validates message-level provider option values as JSON objects and filters wider stable entries during projection. |
| Prompt content parts | `language-model-v4-prompt.ts` | `siumai-spec/src/types/chat/content/part.rs`, `siumai-spec/src/types/ai_sdk.rs` | Green | Stable content now includes `custom`, `reasoning-file`, strict `source`, tool approval fields, request-side `providerOptions`, and first-class provider-owned file/image references via `FilePartSource::ProviderReference`. The V4 provider-facing prompt part overlay uses dedicated text/reasoning/tool-call structures so prompt part `providerOptions` follow upstream `SharedV4ProviderOptions` object-only semantics without narrowing the stable compatibility layer. Public helpers/builders now expose `image_provider_reference` / `file_provider_reference`, OpenAI Chat and OpenAI Responses map those references onto native `file_id` request payloads, Anthropic maps them onto `source:{ type:\"file\", file_id }`, bridge normalization converts incoming OpenAI/Anthropic file ids back into canonical provider references, and the remaining OpenAI `fileIdPrefixes` behavior is only a deprecated provider-runtime compatibility lane rather than a stable prompt-model gap. |
| Prompt data-content helpers | `packages/ai/src/prompt/data-content.ts` | `siumai-spec/src/types/prompt.rs`, `siumai/src/lib.rs` | Green | Shared `DataContent` now exposes the AI SDK helper projections as Rust-style functions: `convert_data_content_to_base64_string(...)`, `convert_data_content_to_uint8_array(...)`, and `convert_uint8_array_to_text(...)`. `convertToLanguageModelV4DataContent` remains a request-converter concern rather than a separate public runtime type because Rust's stable request layer already normalizes shared `DataContent`, URL, and provider-reference payloads through explicit media/file source carriers. |
| Tool-result output | `language-model-v4-prompt.ts` | `siumai-spec/src/types/chat/content/tool_result.rs`, `siumai-spec/src/types/ai_sdk.rs` | Green | The stable `ToolResultOutput` remains backward compatible, while the V4 provider prompt now uses `LanguageModelV4ToolResultOutput` so `text`, `json`, `execution-denied`, `error-text`, `error-json`, and canonical `content` serialize to the upstream prompt contract. `content` intentionally has no output-level `providerOptions`, matching upstream; stable content outputs with supported object-shaped output-level options fall back to valid JSON output rather than leaking an invalid V4 shape, while non-object stable provider option entries are filtered at the V4 projection boundary. OpenAI/OpenAI-compatible tool-message conversion has also been reviewed: the wire contract is string-only, so structured content degrades to a JSON string rather than a lossy flat string. |

## Root export audit

| AI SDK root export | AI SDK reference | Siumai decision | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `generateText` | `packages/ai/src/generate-text/generate-text.ts`, `packages/ai/src/generate-text/generate-text-result.ts` | Implemented as `siumai::generate_text(...)` / `siumai::text::generate_text(...)` | Rust now owns an honest single-step projection over the existing text-family runtime. It does not pretend to be the full AI SDK tool-loop/agent runtime. |
| `embed` / `embedMany` | `packages/ai/src/embed/embed.ts`, `packages/ai/src/embed/embed-many.ts` | Implemented as `siumai::embed(...)` / `siumai::embed_many(...)` plus module helpers | The root helpers return AI SDK-style `EmbedResult` / `EmbedManyResult` while the module keeps raw `embedding::embed(...)` / `embedding::embed_many(...)` for Rust-first response access. |
| `generateImage` | `packages/ai/src/generate-image/generate-image.ts`, `packages/ai/src/generate-image/generate-image-result.ts` | Implemented as root `siumai::generate_image(...)`; raw module helper retained as `siumai::image::generate_image(...)` | The root helper returns `GenerateImageResult` over `GeneratedFile`, warnings, response metadata, provider metadata, and usage. URL-backed legacy provider outputs are materialized on this projection path instead of weakening the AI SDK result shape. |
| `rerank` | `packages/ai/src/rerank/rerank.ts`, `packages/ai/src/rerank/rerank-result.ts` | Implemented as root `siumai::rerank(...)`; raw module helper retained as `siumai::rerank::rerank(...)` | Root returns `RerankResult<JSONValue>` and preserves empty-document short-circuit behavior. Text-only callers can use `siumai::rerank::rerank_text_result(...)`. |
| `generateSpeech` / `transcribe` | `packages/ai/src/generate-speech/generate-speech.ts`, `packages/ai/src/transcribe/transcribe.ts` | Implemented as `siumai::generate_speech(...)` / `siumai::transcribe(...)` plus module helpers | The helper results preserve AI SDK-style warnings, responses, and provider metadata while retaining compatibility mirrors for the older Rust audio fields. |
| `experimental_generateVideo` | `packages/ai/src/generate-video/generate-video.ts`, `packages/ai/src/generate-video/generate-video-result.ts` | Implemented as root `siumai::experimental_generate_video(...)`; raw task helper retained as `siumai::video::generate(...)` | The root helper returns the passive AI SDK-style `GenerateVideoResult` over `GeneratedFile`, warnings, response metadata, and provider metadata. The module helper still exposes completed tasks and Rust-first generated-video assets for callers that need polling/task details. |
| `streamText` / `StreamTextResult` | `packages/ai/src/generate-text/stream-text-result.ts` | Passive result/event carriers implemented; full runtime deferred | `TextStreamPart`, callback events, and stream options are importable, but a real multi-lane `StreamTextResult` needs an explicit Rust tee/backpressure/HTTP design. |
| `createTextStreamResponse` / `pipeTextStreamToResponse` | `packages/ai/src/text-stream/create-text-stream-response.ts`, `packages/ai/src/text-stream/pipe-text-stream-to-response.ts` | Covered on the Axum server-adapter boundary | `siumai-extras::server::axum::to_text_stream_response(...)` and `to_text_stream_response_with_options(...)` provide the Rust equivalent for `ChatStream` -> `text/plain; charset=utf-8` streaming responses. A Node `ServerResponse` pipe helper remains intentionally outside Rust core. |
| `createDownload` / util download helpers | `packages/ai/src/util/download/create-download.ts`, `packages/ai/src/util/download/download.ts`, `packages/provider-utils/src/validate-download-url.ts`, `packages/provider-utils/src/read-response-with-size-limit.ts` | Implemented as Rust utility helpers | Explicit root imports such as `siumai::{create_download, download_url, validate_download_url, read_response_with_size_limit, DEFAULT_MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE}` cover SSRF-style URL validation, inline `data:` downloads, response content-type capture, and 2 GiB default size limiting. These helpers are intentionally not default unified-prelude names. The TypeScript-only `DownloadFunction` callback alias remains a runtime-function pattern rather than a passive data structure. |
| `SerialJobExecutor` | `packages/ai/src/util/serial-job-executor.ts`, `packages/ai/src/util/job.ts` | Implemented as `siumai::SerialJobExecutor` | Rust exposes a cloneable async executor that serializes concurrently submitted jobs through one shared FIFO mutex while preserving each job's return value or error. |
| `AbstractChat` | `packages/ai/src/ui/chat.ts` | Intentionally deferred | This is the stateful browser/client chat controller above `ChatTransport`, not a passive data structure. Siumai should only add an equivalent after it owns a Rust runtime abstraction with matching state transitions. |
| `callCompletionApi` | `packages/ai/src/ui/call-completion-api.ts` | Intentionally deferred | This helper owns browser `fetch`, abort-controller state, UI loading/error callbacks, and text/data stream consumption. Current Rust completion/text helpers cover provider execution, not browser hook transport state. |
| `convertFileListToFileUIParts` | `packages/ai/src/ui/convert-file-list-to-file-ui-parts.ts` | Intentionally deferred | This helper depends on browser `FileList` and `FileReader`; Rust already has file/provider-reference carriers, but not a browser DOM file-list runtime. |
| `gateway` / `createGateway` / `GatewayModelId` | `packages/ai/src/index.ts`, `packages/gateway/src/index.ts`, `packages/gateway/src/gateway-provider.ts` | Intentionally deferred as a separate provider package boundary | AI SDK re-exports the Vercel Gateway provider package from root. Siumai should not add root-level fake exports; any future parity should be a real provider/gateway client with language, embedding, image, video, rerank, metadata, credits, spend, and generation-info behavior. |

## What is still not structurally complete

### 1. Protocol-only replay hints now have an explicit runtime carrier where they are truly protocol-only

OpenAI Responses `rawItem` / `outputIndex` replay is now modeled through a separate runtime replay
carrier attached alongside stable `ChatStreamPart` semantics.

That means:

- `ChatStreamPart` stays semantic
- protocol replay state is not stuffed into generic `providerMetadata`
- same-protocol replay no longer depends on loose provider-scoped custom JSON payloads

Current conclusion after auditing Anthropic against
`repo-ref/ai/packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-messages-language-model.ts`:

- Anthropic reasoning `signature` and `redactedData` are not protocol-only replay state
- AI SDK exposes them on stable `reasoning-*` part `providerMetadata`
- Siumai now follows that same rule

So the dedicated runtime replay carrier remains the right tool for true wire-only fidelity such as
OpenAI Responses `rawItem` / `outputIndex`, but it is no longer the preferred home for Anthropic
reasoning signatures.

### 2. The runtime stream story is structurally correct but still split

Today Siumai has three relevant layers:

- `ChatStreamEvent`
- `ChatStreamPart`
- `TypedStreamPart` / `LanguageModelV4StreamPart`

This is workable, but still more complicated than the AI SDK union story.

Recommendation:

- keep `ChatStreamEvent` as the transport/runtime envelope
- keep `ChatStreamPart` as the primary semantic runtime part
- keep the new `LanguageModelV4Stream*` aliases as the recommended public naming for stream
  payloads in the upgraded overlay
- keep `TypedStreamPart` as a compatibility name, not as the long-term semantic center

### 3. Parser migration is still uneven

The runtime part channel is only fully useful once parsers emit it directly when they already know
the stable meaning.

Current priority order:

1. tighten the remaining transport-hint raw edges and the analogous parse-failure cases outside the now-audited OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini, native OpenAI completion, native Cohere, and native Bedrock first-chunk stream lanes; after re-checking `repo-ref/ai/packages/amazon-bedrock/src/bedrock-chat-language-model.ts`, Bedrock is no longer carrying a known `source` / `custom` stream-part gap because the current upstream `doStream()` contract itself only exposes `stream-start`, `response-metadata`, `raw`, `text-*`, `reasoning-*`, `tool-*`, `finish`, and `error`
2. continue tightening public-path fixture coverage for the remaining OpenAI-compatible raw-hint edges beyond the now-covered metadata/logprobs/prediction-token paths (the Azure model-router placeholder-metadata prelude is now covered)
3. keep auditing provider/runtime coverage around the now-stabilized shared non-chat surface, especially residual provider-owned video knobs
4. keep moving public tests and examples toward `event: part` / stable-part-first assertions so the explicit Axum `{ part, replay }` export contract becomes the default downstream expectation

### 4. Extras orchestration still trails AI SDK in a few high-level controls

The high-level extras step/result surface is now much closer to AI SDK:

- stable `call_id`
- stable `model { provider, model_id }`
- unified `content`
- step-scoped `request` / `response`
- telemetry `function_id` / `metadata`
- stable `raw_finish_reason` backed by `ChatResponse.raw_finish_reason`
- canonical user-defined `context` flowing through `prepare_step`, tool execution, `StepResult`,
  and `on_finish`

The main remaining gaps on this row are now narrower:

- extras still centers the lower-level `messages`, `tool_calls`, and `tool_results` contract even
  though standardized `tool_call_views()` / `tool_result_views()` and static/dynamic splits now
  exist; AI SDK still goes further with stronger type-level tool families
- tool-result projections now resolve `input`, but the stable `ContentPart::ToolResult` itself
  still does not store the full AI SDK typed/dynamic payload directly
- the raw-finish chain is now structurally present on the audited paths because
  `ChatResponse.raw_finish_reason` exists as the stable carrier and extras `StepResult` forwards
  it directly; the remaining work is broader provider coverage review, not missing shared structure

Recommendation:

- keep the newly landed `context`, per-step model override, and normalized tool projections as the
  stable baseline
- continue the next fearless-refactor cut on moving more of those normalized tool semantics into
  the stable content layer before revisiting deeper provider-native finish-reason plumbing
## Recommended next fearless-refactor cuts

### Cut 1 - Split semantic part data from protocol replay hints

Target result:

- stable AI SDK semantics remain in `ChatStreamPart`
- protocol replay hints move into a separate runtime carrier
- serializers stop depending on provider-scoped custom payloads for same-protocol replay

### Cut 2 - Finish parser-side migration to `ChatStreamEvent::Part`

Target result:

- OpenAI-compatible no longer relies on legacy-only transport deltas for tool-call lifecycle semantics
- the remaining parser/protocol bridges become easier to audit because stable semantics share one runtime lane

### Cut 3 - Finish the shared non-chat cleanup pass

Target result:

- shared URL-backed image edit/variation materialization stays centralized at the executor
  boundary instead of drifting back into provider-specific transformers
- Vertex Imagen variation stays on the same shared request lane as the other audited image routes
- the remaining shared video surface stays provider-neutral, with provider-owned knobs continuing
  to move behind typed provider options where needed
